content: This information is not intended to replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always consult your healthcare provider to determine the appropriateness of this information for your specific health needs. Before using nafarelin, carefully read the Medication Guide and any accompanying Patient Information Leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Review these materials each time you receive a refill. Follow the illustrated instructions for the correct use of this medication. If you are using a new bottle, follow the directions for test sprays into the air. Gently blow your nose before administering the medication. Use this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor, typically twice daily (approximately every 12 hours). If more than one spray is required, wait 30 seconds between sprays. Avoid spraying the medication into your eyes. Additionally, avoid sneezing during or immediately after using the medication, as this may reduce the amount absorbed. Follow the detailed instructions for cleaning the spray tip. It is crucial to use this medication consistently and as directed by your doctor. Do not skip doses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist to determine how long each bottle of nasal spray should last. Do not use the bottle beyond the recommended duration, even if medication remains, as you may not receive a full dose. Do not increase your dose or use this medication more frequently or for a longer duration than prescribed. When starting this medication, you may experience a temporary worsening of symptoms (e.g., increased vaginal bleeding for women treating endometriosis, or changes such as increased breast size, pubic hair growth, oily skin, or body odor in children treating early puberty). These symptoms should improve after the first month of treatment. Common side effects in children may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, or vaginal discharge. In women, side effects may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, headaches, decreased sexual interest, muscle pain, vaginal dryness, acne, or a decrease in breast size. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Children using nafarelin may be at risk for increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension). Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using nafarelin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to GnRH or other GnRH-like hormones (e.g., leuprolide), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Women should start this medication between days 2 and 4 of their menstrual cycle. While periods and ovulation may stop during treatment, this is not a reliable form of birth control. Discuss the use of non-hormonal birth control methods (e.g., condoms, diaphragm with spermicide) with your doctor. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not contain all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., tests for pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions), potentially causing false test results. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab and/or medical tests (e.g., growth/bone age velocity in children) should be performed while using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and use your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the bottle upright at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for proper disposal. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
